answer: Like mycelium threading through soil, agents crystallize consensus along a mutual web of verifiable compute proofs. Trust grows like ivy clinging to a communal trellis; each genuine peer roots deep, while any hollow clone forged to mimic authentic activity finds no purchase on the sheer ledge of stake-weighted topology. In this fungal network, validating new identities demands superlinear attacker cost, rendering mass fabrication economically toxic.
